text:
sophie: Quick sync — we need to lock the long-term routing/prioritization anchors for multi-region + tenant isolation. Customer asks piling up; product wants clear launch gates.
maya: High level ask from enterprise sales: data residency + predictable p99 latency in region. They want contractual language for latency & residency by region. :eyes:
raj: For residency, Private/VPC path is straightforward. Multi-region hosted requires routing policy + enforcement. Main infra lift: regional KV cache invalidation + traffic shaping.
kyle: We also need model-aware routing (cheaper model fallback) in the policy matrix. That interacts with tenant isolation — can't leak KV caches across tenancy.
jordan: SLO/monitoring question — do we treat regional p99 as hard SLO or an SLA tier for Dedicated only?
maya: Sales wants it across Dedicated and Hosted for select customers, but understands higher price for strict SLA. We should define a default SLO for Hosted and an enterprise SLA for Dedicated/Private.
sophie: Proposal draft: 1) Default hosted: best-effort regional affinity + 99th percentile target 250ms for small seq length; 2) Dedicated SLA: contractual p99 < 200ms in-region for committed capacity; 3) Private: customer-managed network, SLAs are negotiated.
raj: Tradeoffs: to hit p99 200ms we need reserved capacity + standby capacity for spikes. Also cross-region fallbacks increase tail latency — we need policy precedence: same-region, same-tier, fallback-region.
kyle: Implementation items: routing DSL changes, policy precedence engine, model variant compatibility matrix, telemetry tags for 'affinity' and 'fallback_reason'.
sophie: Launch criteria (proto): - telemetry for affinity/fallback present - routing DSL v1 implemented - regional canary runs (10% traffic) - perf regression tests + guardrail alerts - documented migration path for existing tenants
maya: Add acceptance: customer-facing contract wording and a template for the sales/legal teams.
jordan: Ops: runbook for tenant evacuation if a region overloads. Need automation to shift tenants and a soft-quarantine mode.
raj: Dependencies: infra autoscaler Q2 work, cache invalidation refactor, certs for cross-region comms. Rough estimate: 6-8 sprints across infra + runtime + platform.
kyle: Also require evaluation harness for model fallbacks to track quality degradation on fallback. Redwood Optimize should produce scorecards.
maya: Prioritization ask: Customers A, B name specific iso-required features. Can we propose a phased rollout? Phase 1: regional affinity + SLA templates (low infra change). Phase 2: strict isolation lanes + tenant slices (bigger infra).
sophie: I like phase approach. Phase 1 gates: policy DSL, telemetry, canary. Phase 2 gates: tenant slicing, quota enforcement, eviction playbook.
jordan: Can we add a soft eviction circuit that reduces concurrency for noisy tenants before full eviction?
raj: Yes — implement throttling tiers + degradations first. Full eviction as last resort.
maya: Timeline ask from sales: customers want Q3 pilot. Is Q3 realistic for Phase 1?
kyle: If we scope Phase 1 to affinity + SLA templates + canary, maybe. But need resources: 2 runtime engs, 1 infra, 1 platform, 1 SRE for canary ops.
maya: I'll map customer pilots and negotiate commitment dates.
sophie: Decisions so far: - Move forward with phased plan (Phase 1 = affinity + SLA templates + telemetry/canary). - Build policy precedence DSL and telemetry tags. - Add throttling circuit for noisy tenants. - Draft customer contract templates for SLA/residency.
maya: Action items: Maya -> collect customers for pilots; Raj -> author infra dependencies + spike; Kyle -> RFC for policy DSL; Jordan -> runbook sketch; Sophie -> write RFC + acceptance criteria.
deploy-bot: Note: Created issue RW-PLAT-3147 (Routing DSL RFC) and RW-OPS-2099 (Regional canary run).
sophie: I'll post RFC by EOD Friday. If no blockers, we'll slot Phase 1 into Q3 planning. :thumbsup:
maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
kyle: +1
jordan: +1
raj: +1
